title: Actions and their kinds
line: At the boundary it allows, holds or denies. Every action is granting, destructive or reversible.

words.means: the edge of a computer. Everything that enters or leaves it passes through parts of Silo that run outside it.
one way through the boundary. None exists by default.
data you set. At the boundary it allows, holds or denies. The next film says what triggers it.
what happens to one thing waiting at the boundary: it passes, it waits for your answer, or it is refused.
what a hold shows you: a request that waits for your answer.
to give a computer the ability to do something. Its opposite is to revoke. The words come from access control.
what Silo raises for your attention.
freeze a whole computer: nothing in it runs, nothing crosses its boundary, and nothing is lost. Undone by resume.
end the programs running in a computer. Its disk stays.
a saved moment of a computer. It never changes once saved.
put a computer back to a checkpoint.
a copy of a computer, or of one of its checkpoints, that then lives its own life.
remove a fork. It goes to the bin first.
where a dropped fork waits for a time before it is removed for good.
a value a computer can use and cannot read.

test.question: One rule allows main to reach github.com. A second rule denies anything that carries the secret named deploy-key unless it goes to deploy.example.com. An agent pushes to github.com with that key. What happens, and does it matter which rule you wrote first?
test.answer: The push is denied. One rule allows it and another denies it, and deny beats allow. The order in which you wrote the rules does not matter: rules have no order. The computer keeps running, because a deny forbids one thing only.
